items.note: LVCCA organized 1889 at Larrow Green, creamery 1891, Gideon Vose first president (Story 1).
Gives payment by butterfat test, not weight, but never says the test of the station where the patron delivers governs (a second bolded element).
'under payment by weight, none of what follows would have cost anyone a dollar' (Story 1).
Teague as bookkeeper and Sill as buttermaker named; Effie Loomis absent. This is a list item with no REQUIRED line, so the core fact is enough.
Son of Gideon is right, but it says 'manager from 1911'; the key has 1913 (r23 date drift).
Annual 'station gain' line, fat reaching the creamery beyond what was credited, 'five and a quarter per cent, as usual' (Story 2). No 1898 origin, but that part is unbolded.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896; glass borrowed (Sill's, and the diary's 'done borrowing of Larrow Green').
Section A never describes weighing, the composite sample, the graduated neck or the fixed pipette charge.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice of 14 April 1897, in use from 1 May 1897.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
'a flat 0.19 points, holding steady across every month and season, in winter and summer alike' (Story 2).
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Tester from the opening, twenty-nine seasons; dismissed 30 April 1925 (Story 7).
Station test book in Keddie's hand is named (Stories 3, 7). Only the test book is bolded; the bench-routine detail is context.
Section A gives 3.61 but never the summary leaf's 1896 figure of 3.80. Both figures are required.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, tests rose then fell back, question mark. The 3.80 figure is missing, but this is a list item with no REQUIRED line and the core fact is there.
'Orra's brother Emmet Brant, the largest Hessel Bottom patron'. Orra Keddie is shown as Ansel's wife by the shared household and diary (Stories 5, 7).
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why is absent. Both bolded elements are required.
Died in 1934 with the accusation unresolved (Story 7).
Six farms of Hessel Bottom; Emmet Brant the largest patron.
Weigh book mentioned only as an exhibit: no 1 January 1897 start and no statement that the two scales agreed.
1902 complaint present; 3.61 vs 3.78 kept apart from the 0.19 true shortfall, and the Hollow-vs-Green gap is never stated as 0.19.
Grigg committee sampled January–March 1908 only and concluded wet hay; given as the committee's finding.
Brant's 1910 figure (200,000 lb at 3.42) and the proportional loss appear only in Section C, not in A.
Custody of the weigh book (Roy Brant 1929, lent to Ivy 1958) not given.
Only 'Alder Corners cheese factory (over the ridge)'. No Redlow Ridge, Vessey County or Jerome Cudd.
Four Hessel Bottom farms hauled there in summer, 1915–1930.
Section A names the Cudd records (one element) but gives no second one: not the other county, bench or glassware, nor the uncompared book.
Same four farms tested 3.78–3.82 there across sixteen summers, 1915–1930, against the station's 3.61.
Same farms tested normally over the ridge, 'the deficiency traveled with the Ostrey Hollow station, not with the hay or the cows'.
Rosalie Cudd named only as the source of records; not Jerome's daughter, and no copying of sixteen seasons for Ivy.
Merle Strawn named, but the circuit and lactometer run 'from 1908 onward' (NT-23); the key has 1907–1936.
Lactometer at every visit never once found added water at the station.
12 June 1923, against a calibrated burette, condemned the entire lot.
Never says Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report.
Says the average 'immediately rose to 3.85% and held there'; the key has 3.80. No 28 June / 2 July dates.
Crate to the loft is given, but not the notebooks' route to the college library in 1947. Both bolded elements are required.
Petition of January 1925.
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March – 4 May 1925, two of three sittings at the station.
Heard watering, skimming and wet hay; found none proven.
Four exhibits listed, including the inspector's notebook, but not that it held the answer and was read only for its other lines (a bolded element).
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no theory proven; award $3,800 'without admission'. The account it was charged to is A7.6's aspect.
Section A never gives the award as one fifth of $19,000 or says it was charged to the station-gain account.
Granddaughter; graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland; Leland Vaught.
Section A never says she assembled records that had never been in the same room.
February 1958, crate in the loft, nine surviving pipettes.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 against a marked 17.6, 'about 5% short'.
Recorded 3.61 against a true 3.80, flat 0.19, from the 5%-short glass used 1897–1923 (Stories 1, 2, 8).
Section A has none of 40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 or the ledger identity.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clearing him 'twenty-four years after his death'. The 35 and 33 are missing, but this is a list item with no REQUIRED line.
Granddaughter.
Derived from Duncan as Ansel's son and Ivy as Duncan's daughter (r18); r22's correction noted.
Second cousins, derived through Emmet/Orra as siblings and Roy/Duncan as first cousins.
A08 not addressed. Claims 'the sources leave nothing substantial open'; never says full vs half siblings cannot be determined. It asserts neither side, so no deduction.
Gideon Vose; nephew rumour rebutted.
Significance given as 'institutional insider by birth'. No link to Article VII making the test decisive, and no Vose Jerseys point.
'The sources do not establish any real connection… the documents cannot fully prove the absence of one'. No verdict sentence that they were or were not kin, so it counts as an abstention.
Says only one witness asserts kinship (the key has two), treats the family denial as the best evidence, and never says no document names or denies a link.
$90.00 with working, explicitly using the whole-period average of 25¢; the key's stated exception applies.
76,000 lb; 5.26% of credited and 5.00% of delivered, denominators named.
$77.93 by addition.
72 pipettes, each 0.88 c.c. short.
Gives '26 calendar years' for the glass in use; the key requires 26 years and 6 weeks (or an exact equivalent). The 25 full years and the reason are right, but the first figure is not exact.
Abstention item A02: asserts 'an estimated 1,100,000 lb' (r23's pole) instead of saying it cannot be determined.
Variable is the measuring instrument (own glass vs borrowed), 8 May – 10 July.
Held constant: tester, herds, pasture, season.
Says only that tests 'rose' and 'fell back'. No 3.80 and no 3.61.
Tracked the instrument, not the cows or the tester; limit: no cubic centimetres or size measured in 1911.
1911 interval (r22, r24), ledger surplus (r05, r14, r23), Alder Corners (r10): three reasons from at least three narrators.
Independence argued; the ledger surplus named as holding without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention item A09: 'On the substance, though: no', based on Kyle's 'never asked anybody anything'. That is an assertion.
'almost certainly knew the station's tests ran chronically low', with the 1919 circular.
Only two of the five clearly present (1919 circular; signing the sheets). Gives manager from 1911 instead of 1913; no watering argued at the hearing; nothing on his never naming the glassware.
Never declares the understatement question unsettleable ('no clear evidence of awareness'), and lacks the two required observations. No verdict sentence, so no deduction.
Pairs resolved with a stated method but without naming both carriers: 16.72 vs 16.27 (arithmetic), 3.61 vs 3.16 (majority), $3,800 vs $3,500 (documents), award year 1925 vs 1924. Capped at 3.

Pairs named with both carriers and a stated tie-breaker: NT-10 (r11, r23; invoice + diary), NT-11 (r08, r12; r06), NT-14 (r19, r20; itemized addition), NT-18 (r19, r22; r18 + r22 retraction), NT-22 (r15, r16; D12 quoted by r22). Capped at 3. NT-16 is miscredited to r12/r18 and not counted.
None of A04, A06, A10 identified as unsettleable.
Identifies r20 printing $77.39 above its own itemized invoice summing to $77.93: a self-refutation on the page.

1897 pipettes, 16.72 vs 17.6, 5%; 0.19 is 5% of 3.80; onset 1 May 1897 and cessation 12 June 1923 with nothing on the farms changing. The 3.85 cessation figure is unbolded and is charged as a deduction.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer readings.
Theft defeated by the heavy cream in the ledger and by the 1911 interval.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter and nothing in summer vs a flat 0.19, and by Alder Corners.
Abstention item A07: 'The 1925 board of arbitration never examined the condemned glassware'. Asserted.
Abstention item A05: 'The tester himself privately believed… that the cause was something in the glass'. Asserted on r18's pole.
Summary is about 167 words; the limit is 150.
Only four record series identifiable (invoice, hearing record, ledgers, 1958 measurement); five required.
No decoy adopted and no wrong headline figure in the summary.
About 5% low, 1897, 1923, 1958: four elements covering both ends (names and 76,000 lb absent).

deductions.reason: Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 (r23 X94), asserted in Story 5 and D3
Corruption: Strawn's circuit/lactometer from 1908 (NT-23), asserted in Story 5 and F
Corruption: post-1923 / 1924 average of 3.85 (NT-3 / X90), asserted in Story 8, C1(b) and F1
Gullibility: A02 asserted (1896 intake 1,100,000 lb, C5b)
Gullibility: A09 asserted (bookkeeper never questioned the entries, D2)
Gullibility: A07 asserted (board never examined the glassware, F and Story 7)
Gullibility: A05 asserted (tester believed it was the glass, F and Story 3)
